title: Swahili Coconut Beef Curry
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Swahili Coconut Beef Curry — tender beef simmered in a rich, fragrant sauce of coconut milk, tomatoes, and coastal spices. Where mainland beef curry uses water-based stock, this coastal version adds thick coconut milk for a creamier, sweeter, more aromatic result.
longDesc: Swahili coconut beef curry is what happens when the inland beef curry tradition meets the coast's beloved coconut milk. The result is richer, creamier, and more complex than either alone — the coconut's natural sweetness balancing the warm spices while the beef's depth enriches the coconut sauce. Served with coconut rice, it is the coastal celebration meal for meat lovers.
steps: Brown beef in batches in hot oil. Remove and set aside.
Cook onions until deeply golden — 10 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook for 8—10 minutes until very thick.
Add all spices except garam masala. Stir 1 minute.
Return beef. Add stock. Cover and simmer 60—70 minutes until tender.
Add coconut milk. Stir gently. Simmer on low for 15 minutes — do not boil hard.
Stir in garam masala. Garnish with coriander.
chefTips: Add coconut milk only after the beef is tender — too early and the long cooking splits it.
The sauce should be thick before adding coconut milk.
Gentle final simmer after coconut milk — 15 minutes maximum.
commonMistakes: Boiling hard after adding coconut milk.
cookingScience: Coconut milk is added at the end because extended boiling breaks the emulsion. Brief gentle simmering integrates the flavours without splitting.
sustainabilityTips: Stewing cuts are sustainable — tougher muscles that improve with slow cooking.
reheating: Gently on stovetop — add splash of coconut milk if needed.
culturalNote: Coconut beef curry is a celebrated dish of the Swahili coast — the meeting of two great culinary traditions: the East African beef stew and the coastal coconut milk that transforms everything it touches.
